title: Machine learning builds a blood DNA methylation risk score for cognitive impairment
summary: Using whole-blood genome-wide DNA methylation as a surrogate for 14 dementia risk factors, machine learning produced a multivariate methylation risk score that identified mild cognitive impairment cross-sectionally independent of age and sex (P = 2.0 x 10-3). In independent studies it predicted cognitive impairment, with hazard ratios of 2.47 for RAVLT-Learning in Alzheimer's disease and 2.59 for MCI/dementia in Parkinson's disease.
ai_technology: Machine learning models combining methylation data into a multivariate risk score

evidence.unknown: Association-level evidence; clinical utility not shown; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: ML derives the composite score from methylation data.
